description:
This C# class, TextFormatter.Class1, provides a method to format text into various case styles based on a given caseType. It defines a static method FormatText that takes two parameters: text (the string to be formatted) and caseType (the format style). Here's a breakdown of the supported case types:

"sentence": Capitalizes the first letter of the sentence while making the rest lowercase.
"title": Capitalizes the first letter of each word in the string.
"uppercase": Converts the entire string to uppercase.
"lowercase": Converts the entire string to lowercase.
"capitalized": Capitalizes the first letter of each word and makes the rest lowercase.
"camel": Converts the string to camelCase (the first word is lowercase, and each subsequent word starts with an uppercase letter).
"pascal": Converts the string to PascalCase (similar to camelCase but with the first letter of the first word also capitalized).
"snake": Converts the string to snake_case, where spaces are replaced with underscores and all characters are lowercase.
"kebab": Converts the string to kebab-case, where spaces are replaced with hyphens and all characters are lowercase.
"alternating": Alternates between lowercase and uppercase letters for each character in the string.
The method throws an exception if the text is null or empty, or if the caseType is invalid (not one of the supported formats).

This class is useful for formatting text in a UI where the user might need to choose from multiple text-case formatting options.

Initial Release of the TextFormatter package.
This version includes a single class, Class1, with a method FormatText that supports multiple text formatting styles:
Sentence Case
Title Case
Uppercase
Lowercase
Capitalized Case
Camel Case
Pascal Case

Alternating Case
Highlights:
The FormatText method takes a string and a case type (caseType) as input and returns the text in the specified format.
Supports handling of edge cases such as null, empty, or whitespace input with error messages.
Provides user-friendly error handling for invalid case types.
